target_customer: Online businesses that must verify user identity, including banks, fintechs, marketplaces, mobility and gig economy companies
problem: Online services needed to verify who users are across many countries and document types without losing customers to friction or letting fraudsters through.
business_model: Usage-based API: monthly platform fee plus a fee per verification

founders.name: Kaarel Kotkas
previous_startups: Two earlier startups (TechCrunch 2018 says Veriff was his third startup; names not given)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch June 2018 says he was 23 at the time and developed the idea at TransferWise; Wikipedia says he created Veriff after altering his ID birth year to pass a PayPal check. Education not found.

founders.name: Janer Gorohhov
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Wikipedia and Silicon Canals; the YC page lists only Kotkas.

competitors.name: Onfido
competitors.what: Document and selfie based identity verification API recognizing about 600 document formats
competitors.funding_then: $30M Series C in September 2017, over $60M raised in total

technical_complexity.rationale: Document recognition, face matching and fraud detection across many countries need machine learning and operations at scale, though the 2018 product was API integration over existing vision techniques.

defensibility.rationale: Many vendors sold similar document and selfie checks, and TechCrunch notes a number of competitors. Volume data and bank integrations help but do not block rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not buy or copy Veriff; it stayed independent, raised a $100M Series C in 2022, and later acquired Vespia in February 2026 per a trade report.

market_need_then: Online banks, fintechs and sharing economy firms were onboarding users remotely and needed fast identity checks; TechCrunch in June 2018 reported over 40 paying customers and pricing of 49 euros per month plus 2 euros per verification.

branding.domain_note: Uses veriff.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: New logo and color palette introduced in August 2022 inspired by ID document security features
identity.visual_style: Patterns inspired by security features on identity documents, illustration system
identity.voice_and_tone: Trust and mission oriented, a company podcast covers how it found its voice

rebrands.to: Elevated brand identity with new logo, patterns and illustration system
rebrands.why: Reflect the company's continued growth and its mission of rebuilding trust online, per the press release.

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press coverage of the brand update; no merch or fan community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in identity verification and by YC and fintech buyers, with deliberate brand work in 2022; no evidence of brand-led growth.

outcome_analysis: Veriff began serving Estonian banks in 2016, joined YC in W18 and raised a $7.7M Series A in June 2018, then $69M in April 2021 and $100M at a $1.5B valuation in January 2022 as remote onboarding boomed. It cut staff in 2020 and 2023 (a 2023 report counts about one fifth of the workforce) but remains independent, with about 600 employees on the YC page and an acquisition of Vespia in 2026.
notes: Series B amount and investors are from Wikipedia and search snippets of trade outlets (Sorainen, FinTech Futures), not opened. Bridge funding in June 2020 reported as about 13.8M euros by Wikipedia and $15.5M by an aggregator, led by NordicNinja per one source; not recorded as a round due to conflict. Initial investor in 2016 was Inbank per Wikipedia, no amount. Wikipedia says $1.3B valuation in text but the cited release says $1.5B. Total raised conflicts: company says $200M, Wikipedia says $92.8M. Onfido source (September 2017) is dated before the batch; TechCrunch on Veriff names no competitors.
